title: Robust Covariance and Sparse Robust Estimation

items.title: Covariance matrix of a finite-dimensional random vector

references.title: Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 4

items.statement:
Let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_p)$ be a measurable random vector in $\mathbb R^p$,
where $p\ge1$ is finite, and assume $\mathbb E\|X\|_2^2<\infty$. Define
the mean coordinatewise by $\mu_j=\mathbb E X_j$ and define the covariance
matrix by
$$\Sigma:=\mathbb E[(X-\mu)(X-\mu)^T],$$
where each entry is the expectation of the corresponding real random
variable. Write $\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^p\Sigma_{jj}$.

The well-definedness lemma proves these expectations are finite,
$\Sigma$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and
$\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)=\mathbb E\|X-\mu\|_2^2$.

items.title: Finite-dimensional Golden–Thompson trace inequality
items.statement:
For Hermitian matrices $H,K\in\mathbb C^{p\times p}$ with $p\ge1$,
$$\operatorname{tr}\exp(H+K)\le\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\exp(H)\exp(K)\bigr).$$
Here $\exp(A)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}A^j/j!$ is the norm-convergent finite-matrix exponential series. No commutativity assumption is imposed.

references.title: Joel A. Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, §3.3, equation (3.3.3), printed p.34

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Proposition 3.1

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the standard-normal-law definition. The continuity, symmetry, strict monotonicity and intermediate-value argument uses no additional choice.
items.statement:
Let $\Phi(t)=N(0,1)((-\infty,t])$. There is a unique $\beta>0$ such that
$\Phi(\sqrt\beta)=3/4$.

items.title: Uniform deviation for squared-projection slabs

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Lemma 7.3
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 4

items.statement:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be independent random elements of $\mathbb R^p$ with
common Borel probability law $P$. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_m\subseteq[p]$ be
nonempty coordinate sets with $|S_j|\le s$, where $m,s\ge1$, and define
$$V_{S_j}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\|u\|_2=1,\ u_i=0\text{ for }i\notin S_j\}.$$
For $u\in V_{S_j}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, put
$A_{u,t}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^p:|u^Tx|^2\le t\}$ and
$P_N(A):=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}$. There is a universal
constant $C$ such that, for every $0<\delta<1$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\max_{1\le j\le m}\sup_{\substack{u\in V_{S_j}\\t\in\mathbb R}}|P_N(A_{u,t})-P(A_{u,t})|\le C\left[\sqrt{\frac{s+1}{N}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(m/\delta)}{N}}\right]\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
The same bound holds for the upper-tail sets
$\{x:|u^Tx|^2\ge t\}$.

items.title: Bounded-spectrum covariance class

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §3.2

items.statement:
For $M>0$ and $p\ge1$, define
$$\mathcal F_p(M):=\{\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}: \Sigma=\Sigma^T,\ \Sigma\succeq0,\ \|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}\le M\}.$$
For positive semidefinite $\Sigma$, the operator norm is its largest
eigenvalue, so this is the bounded-spectrum covariance class.

items.title: Matrix variance for covariance estimation

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §2

items.statement:
For a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^p$ with mean $\mu$ and covariance
$\Sigma$ as in [[def-covariance-matrix-of-a-random-vector]], assume
$\mathbb E\|X-\mu\|_2^4<\infty$. Its **matrix variance** is
$$\sigma_0^2:=\left\|\mathbb E\!\left[\|X-\mu\|_2^2 (X-\mu)(X-\mu)^T\right]\right\|_{\rm op}.$$
When $\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}>0$, define the intrinsic ratio
$$d:=\frac{\sigma_0^2}{\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2}.$$

The expectation is entrywise. The finite fourth moment makes every entry
integrable. This definition imposes neither Huber contamination nor sample
replacement.

items.title: Bounded independent matrix Bernstein bound from the trace exponential
items.statement:
Let $B_1,\ldots,B_m$ be independent centered random Hermitian $q\times q$ matrices, $q,m\ge1$. Suppose $R>0$, $v\ge0$, and
$$\|B_i\|_{\rm op}\le R\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad\|\mathbb E B_i^2\|_{\rm op}\le v\quad(1\le i\le m).$$
Writing $Y=\sum_{i=1}^m B_i$, for $0<s<3/R$ one has
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\exp(sY)\le q\exp\left(\frac{ms^2v}{2(1-sR/3)}\right).$$
Consequently, for $u>0$ when $v>0$,
$$\mathbb P\{\lambda_{\max}(Y)\ge u\}\le q\exp\left(-\frac{u^2}{2(mv+Ru/3)}\right).$$
For every $b>0$, the following convenient forms also hold:
$$\mathbb P\left\{\lambda_{\max}(Y)>\sqrt{2mvb}+\frac{2Rb}{3}\right\}\le qe^{-b},\qquad\mathbb P\left\{\|Y\|_{\rm op}>\sqrt{2mvb}+\frac{2Rb}{3}\right\}\le2qe^{-b}.$$
If $v=0$, all $B_i$ and $Y$ vanish almost surely, so the displayed positive-threshold conclusions remain valid.

references.title: Joel A. Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, §§3.2–3.3 and §§6.6–6.7, especially Lemma 6.6.2

items.title: A finite second moment defines a positive semidefinite covariance matrix

references.title: Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 4

items.statement:
If $X\in\mathbb R^p$ is measurable and $\mathbb E\|X\|_2^2<\infty$, then
$\mu=\mathbb E X$ and $\Sigma=\mathbb E[(X-\mu)(X-\mu)^T]$ in
[[def-covariance-matrix-of-a-random-vector]] are well-defined entrywise,
$\Sigma$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and
$\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)=\mathbb E\|X-\mu\|_2^2$.

items.title: Adaptive truncated covariance estimator
items.statement:
Input a finite sample $X_1,\ldots,X_m\in\mathbb R^p$, confidence
parameter $\beta>1$, and positive finite scale bounds
$0<\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_{\max}$. The computational domain requires
$k=\lfloor3.5\beta\rfloor+1\le m/2$. Statistical guarantees are stated
separately: for a clean iid finite-fourth-moment law, use the matrix variance
of [[def-matrix-variance-of-a-random-vector]] and a bracket containing
$\sigma_0$. The statistical conditions are not needed merely to evaluate this
finite-sample procedure.

Call [[alg-geometric-median-of-block-means]] on $(X_1,\ldots,X_m)$
with block count $k$ to obtain the pilot $\widehat\mu$. Use its consecutive
blocks in index order, of size $\lfloor m/k\rfloor+1$ for the first
$m-k\lfloor m/k\rfloor$ blocks and $\lfloor m/k\rfloor$ for the rest.
This uses the same sample and is not a sample split.

For a real symmetric matrix $A=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)Q^T$, define
$\psi(A)=Q\operatorname{diag}(\psi(\lambda_i))Q^T$, where
$\psi(x)=\operatorname{sign}(x)\min(|x|,1)$. The real spectral theorem
makes this definition independent of the chosen orthonormal eigenbasis.
Define the finite grid and truncation thresholds
$$\sigma_j=2^j\sigma_{\min},\qquad J=\{j\in\mathbb Z:\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_j<2\sigma_{\max}\},\qquad \theta_j=\frac1{\sigma_j}\sqrt{\frac\beta m}.$$
For every $j\in J$, form
$$\widehat\Sigma_{m,j} =\frac1{m\theta_j}\sum_{i=1}^m \psi\!\left(\theta_j(X_i-\widehat\mu)(X_i-\widehat\mu)^T\right).$$
Choose the smallest $j^*\in J$ such that
$$\|\widehat\Sigma_{m,k'}-\widehat\Sigma_{m,j^*}\|_{\rm op} \le6\sigma_{k'}\sqrt{\frac\beta m} \quad\text{for every }k'\in J,\ k'>j^*,$$
and output $\widehat\Sigma^*=\widehat\Sigma_{m,j^*}$.

This is the clean heavy-tail moment procedure. It makes no Huber
contamination or sample-replacement guarantee.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §2

items.title: Single-block sparse covariance class and restricted directions

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §3.4

items.statement:
For $S\subseteq[p]$, let
$$G(S):=\{A=A^T\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}:A_{ij}=0 \text{ whenever }i\notin S\text{ or }j\notin S\},$$
and, for an integer $1\le s\le p$, let
$$G(s):=\bigcup_{\substack{S\subseteq[p]\\|S|\le s}}G(S),\qquad \mathcal F_{p,s}(M):=\{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M): \Sigma-\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma)\in G(s)\}.$$
Here $\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma)$ is the diagonal matrix with the same
diagonal entries as $\Sigma$. Thus all nonzero off-diagonal entries lie in
one common coordinate block of size at most $s$; no row-sparsity condition
is implied.

For $S\subseteq[p]$, define
$$V_S:=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\|u\|_2=1,\ u_i=0\text{ for }i\notin S\}.$$
When $1\le s\le p/2$, the restricted direction set is
$$U_s:=\bigcup_{\substack{S\subseteq[p]\\|S|=2s}}V_S.$$

items.title: Gaussian Huber contamination model for covariance estimation

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §2

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the published finite-dimensional Gaussian-law construction to supply $N_p(0,\Sigma);$ the mixture definition itself makes no further choice.
items.statement:
Let $p\ge1$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real positive
semidefinite $p\times p$ covariance matrix. For any Borel probability law
$Q$ on $\mathbb R^p$, define
$$P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}:=(1-\epsilon)N_p(0,\Sigma)+\epsilon Q,$$
where $N_p(0,\Sigma)$ is the finite-dimensional Gaussian law from
[[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. A sample in this model consists of
independent observations with common law $P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$. The target
is the covariance $\Sigma$ of the uncontaminated Gaussian component, not the
covariance of the mixture.

This is the covariance specialization of the Huber model in
[[def-huber-contamination-model]]. It is distinct from a clean heavy-tail
moment model and from adversarial sample replacement.

items.title: Exact block budget for the covariance geometric-median pilot
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m\in\mathbb R^p$ be iid with
mean $\mu$, finite covariance $\Sigma$, and $T=\operatorname{tr}\Sigma$.
For $\beta>1$, put $k=\lfloor3.5\beta\rfloor+1\le m/2$. Partition the
sample deterministically into $k$ blocks whose sizes differ by at most one,
and let $\widehat\mu$ be the minimum-norm geometric median of the block
means as in [[alg-geometric-median-of-block-means]]. Then
$$P\!\left(\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2>11\sqrt{\frac{T(\beta+1)}m}\right)\le e^{-\beta}.$$
In particular the larger radius $B=11\sqrt{2T\beta/m}$ has the same
failure bound. This uses the prescribed covariance-pilot block count,
without changing the robust-mean theorem's separate confidence convention.

references.title: Minsker and Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions

items.title: The covariance matrix variance ratio is at least one

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §2
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 4

items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; one top eigenvector is supplied by the finite-dimensional spectral theorem.
items.statement:
Let $X\in\mathbb R^p$ have finite fourth moment, mean $\mu$, nonzero
covariance $\Sigma$, and matrix variance $\sigma_0^2$ as in
[[def-covariance-matrix-of-a-random-vector]] and
[[def-matrix-variance-of-a-random-vector]]. Then
$$d:=\frac{\sigma_0^2}{\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2}\ge1.$$

items.title: Oracle-truncated covariance and vector concentration under finite matrix variance
items.statement:
Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ be independent copies of a centered random vector $Z\in\mathbb R^p$, $p,m\ge1$, with nonzero covariance $\Sigma=\mathbb E ZZ^T$ and finite fourth moment. Write
$$T=\operatorname{tr}\Sigma,\qquad\sigma_0^2=\left\|\mathbb E[\|Z\|_2^2ZZ^T]\right\|_{\rm op}.$$
For $\beta>1$, $\sigma\ge\sigma_0$, and $t=\beta/m$, set
$$\theta=\frac{\sqrt t}{\sigma},\qquad R=\frac1\theta,\qquad w(z)=\min\left\{1,\frac{R}{\|z\|_2^2}\right\},\qquad w(0)=1,$$
$$S=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m w(Z_i)Z_iZ_i^T,\qquad V=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m w(Z_i)Z_i.$$
Then there are events $E_S,E_V$ such that
$$\mathbb P(E_S^c)\le pe^{-\beta},\qquad\mathbb P(E_V^c)\le\frac{p+1}{2}e^{-\beta},$$
and on the respective events
$$\|S-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}\le\left(2+\frac{\log2}{\beta}\right)\sigma\sqrt t<\frac{27}{10}\sigma\sqrt t,$$
$$\|V\|_2\le\sigma_0\sqrt\theta+2\sqrt{Tt}+\frac{8t}{3\sqrt\theta}.$$
The same $S$ also has the sharper-radius, larger-failure alternative
$$\mathbb P\left\{\|S-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}>\left(\sqrt2+\frac23+\frac14\right)\sigma\sqrt t\right\}\le2pe^{-\beta}.$$
No independence between these events and a statistic formed from the same sample is asserted or needed.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §§5.3–5.5
Joel A. Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, §§6.6–6.7

items.title: Matrix depth and covariance estimators

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §3.1

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the Gaussian scale constant beta. The definition returns the full argmax correspondence and selects no matrix.
items.statement:
For $p\ge1$, write $S^{p-1}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\|u\|_2=1\}$. Let
$U$ be a nonempty subset of this sphere, let $P$ be a probability law on
$\mathbb R^p$, and let $\Gamma\succeq0$. Its **matrix depth relative to
$U$** is
$$D_U(\Gamma,P):=\inf_{u\in U}\min\left\{ P((u^TX)^2\le u^T\Gamma u),P((u^TX)^2\ge u^T\Gamma u)\right\},$$
where $X$ has law $P$. Both weak inequalities include ties.

For observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, let
$$P_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{x_i}$$
on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^p$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]).
Each Dirac measure is a probability measure by [[def-dirac-measure]] and
[[prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure]]. Their finite nonnegative
weighted sum is a measure by [[def-nonnegative-weighted-sum-of-measures]]
and [[thm-nonnegative-weighted-sums-of-measures]], and its total mass is
$n^{-1}\sum_i1=1$; hence $P_n$ is a probability law by
[[def-probability-measure]]. Let $\beta>0$ be the constant of
[[lem-matrix-depth-gaussian-scale-constant-exists-uniquely]].
The **global dense** depth correspondence is $\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\succeq0}D_{S^{p-1}}(\Gamma,P_n)$, over symmetric positive semidefinite matrices. For $1\le s\le p/2$, define the global single-block class $\mathcal F_{p,s}:=\bigcup_{c>0}\mathcal F_{p,s}(c)$ and the **global single-block sparse** correspondence $\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}}D_{U_s}(\Gamma,P_n)$. These are the unrestricted-spectrum versions; no known spectral bound is needed to define their selectors.

For known $M>0$, the dense bounded-class depth correspondence is
$$\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\in\mathcal F_p(\beta M)} D_{S^{p-1}}(\Gamma,P_n).$$
For known integer $1\le s\le p/2$, the single-block sparse version is
$$\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(\beta M)} D_{U_s}(\Gamma,P_n),$$
where the classes and $U_s$ are defined in
[[def-bounded-spectrum-covariance-class]] and
[[def-block-sparse-covariance-class]]. A **measurable matrix-depth estimator**
is a Borel measurable selector $\widehat\Gamma$ from the applicable argmax
correspondence, with covariance output $\widehat\Sigma=\widehat\Gamma/\beta$.
Either global correspondence or the applicable bounded-class correspondence may be used. The compact search restriction contains $\beta\Sigma$ whenever the target
belongs to the corresponding class; it makes no computational feasibility
claim.

items.title: The adaptive truncated covariance procedure is well-defined on its declared domain
items.statement:
On the input domain in [[alg-adaptive-truncated-covariance-estimator]], the
adaptive truncated covariance procedure is total and Borel measurable as a
function of the sample.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §2

items.title: Fixed-scale matrix-truncated covariance deviation under finite matrix variance
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the specified geometric-median pilot. Let
$X_i\in\mathbb R^p$, $1\le i\le m$, be iid with mean $\mu$, nonzero
covariance $\Sigma$, finite fourth central moment and matrix variance
$\sigma_0^2$ as in [[def-matrix-variance-of-a-random-vector]]. Put
$$L=\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op},\quad T=\operatorname{tr}\Sigma,\quad d=\sigma_0^2/L^2,\quad D=\max\{d,(T/\sigma_0)^2\}.$$
For $\sigma\ge\sigma_0$, $\beta>1$ set $t=\beta/m$,
$\theta=\sqrt t/\sigma$ and
$$\widehat\Sigma_\theta=\frac1{m\theta}\sum_i\psi\!\left(\theta(X_i-\widehat\mu)(X_i-\widehat\mu)^{\mathsf T}\right).$$
For any measurable pilot, any $B\ge0$ and any event $E$ on which
$\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|\le B$, there is an event $G$ with
$P(G^c)\le h_p e^{-\beta}$, $h_p=(3p+1)/2$, such that on $E\cap G$,
$$\|\widehat\Sigma_\theta-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}\le a_0\sigma\sqrt t+qM+2B(W+q\sqrt M)+B^2,$$
where $a_0=27/10$, $q=2B\sqrt\theta+B^2\theta$,
$M=L+a_0\sigma\sqrt t$ and
$W=\sigma_0\sqrt\theta+2\sqrt{Tt}+8t/(3\sqrt\theta)$.
The concentration event is constructed from the true centered observations
and the inequality is uniform over the pilot ball; no independence of the
pilot and sample is assumed.

For the exact pilot of [[alg-adaptive-truncated-covariance-estimator]], the
explicit sufficient sample condition
$$m\ge10^{16}D\beta$$
therefore gives
$$P\!\left(\|\widehat\Sigma_\theta-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}>3\sigma\sqrt{\beta/m}\right)\le(h_p+1)e^{-\beta}\le5p e^{-\beta}.$$
Every finite-fourth-moment law is retained under this trace-aware sample
condition; no coordinate independence or bounded-kurtosis assumption is
added. If the mean is supplied exactly, the stronger bound
$2.7\sigma\sqrt{\beta/m}$ holds with failure at most $p e^{-\beta}$ for
every $m\ge1$, without the $D$ sample condition.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, Lemma 2.1 and §§4.1–4.2

items.title: The Gaussian Huber covariance mixture is a probability law

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §2

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited only from the Gaussian-law supplier in the model definition; the convex-mixture calculation is choice-free.
items.statement:
For every admissible $p,\epsilon,\Sigma,Q$ in
[[def-huber-covariance-model]], $P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$ is a probability
measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb R^p$.

items.title: Lepski scale selection transfers fixed-scale covariance bounds
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma\ne0$, $\sigma_0>0$, $m\ge1$, $\beta>1$ and
$0<\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_0\le\sigma_{\max}$. Use the finite grid and
agreement rule of [[alg-adaptive-truncated-covariance-estimator]], with
measurable matrix estimates on that grid. Put
$$L_g=\log_2(2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}),\quad J=\{0,\ldots,\lceil L_g\rceil-1\},\quad \bar j=\left\lceil\log_2(\sigma_0/\sigma_{\min})\right\rceil,\quad N_+=\lceil L_g\rceil-\bar j.$$
On any event on which every $j\ge\bar j$ satisfies
$\|\widehat\Sigma_j-\Sigma\|\le3\sigma_j\sqrt{\beta/m}$, the selected
estimate satisfies $\|\widehat\Sigma^*-\Sigma\|<18\sigma_0\sqrt{\beta/m}$.
If the individual failures are at most $q_j$, its success probability is at
least $1-\sum_{j\ge\bar j}q_j$. For the prescribed same-sample estimator,
when the hypotheses of [[lem-fixed-scale-truncated-covariance-deviation]]
hold at every required scale, its individual failure bounds
$q_j=5p e^{-\beta}$ give success probability at least
$1-5p\lceil L_g\rceil e^{-\beta}$. The shared-event bound below counts the
common pilot failure once.

More sharply, suppose a common event $E$ has $P(E^c)\le\delta$, and for
each $j\ge\bar j$ an event $G_j$ has $P(G_j^c)\le h e^{-\beta}$, with
the stated fixed-scale bound valid on $E\cap G_j$. Then success is at
least $1-\delta-hN_+e^{-\beta}$. No independence between scales or the
pilot and covariance estimates is required. The exact grid cardinality is
$\lceil L_g\rceil$, not the generally false unrounded bound $|J|\le L_g$.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, Theorem 2.1 and §4.3

items.title: A matrix-depth maximizer exists on the bounded covariance classes

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §3.1 and §3.2

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through beta in the estimator definition. The compactness and upper-semicontinuity proof itself is choice-free.
items.statement:
For every integer $p\ge1$, every nonempty finite sample in $\mathbb R^p$,
and every $M>0$, the dense bounded-class argmax correspondence
$$\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\in\mathcal F_p(\beta M)}D_{S^{p-1}}(\Gamma,P_n)$$
from [[def-matrix-depth-covariance-estimator]] is nonempty compact. If
$1\le s\le p/2$, the single-block sparse bounded-class argmax
$$\operatorname{Argmax}_{\Gamma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(\beta M)}D_{U_s}(\Gamma,P_n)$$
is also nonempty compact.

items.title: The scaled Gaussian covariance has matrix depth at least one half

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Proposition 3.1

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the finite-dimensional Gaussian-law supplier. The one-dimensional probability calculation is choice-free.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma\succeq0$, let $U\subseteq S^{p-1}$ be nonempty, and let
$N_p(0,\Sigma)$ be its centered Gaussian law. If $\beta$ is the unique
positive constant satisfying $\Phi(\sqrt\beta)=3/4$, then
$$D_U(\beta\Sigma,N_p(0,\Sigma))\ge\frac12.$$
Equality holds for every direction with positive variance; when $\Sigma=0$
the depth is $1$.

items.title: Huber covariance modulus lower bound for unrestricted matrix-valued actions

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §5 and supplement
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 5, §5.3

items.axiom_use: AC is required by the Huber mixture equalization supplier. All other steps are finite-product identities or pointwise triangle inequalities and use no further choice.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $p,n\ge1$, $M>0$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and let $\Theta$ be
either $\mathcal F_p(M)$ from [[def-bounded-spectrum-covariance-class]] or
$\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)$ from [[def-block-sparse-covariance-class]] with
$1\le s\le p/2$, equipped with its induced Borel sigma-algebra. Let
$\mathscr E_n$ be the set of Borel maps
$(\mathbb R^p)^n\to\mathbb R^{p\times p}$. The clean family is
$P_\Sigma=N_p(0,\Sigma)$. For $\Sigma\in\Theta$ and matrix action $A$, put
$$\ell(\Sigma,A)=\|\Sigma-A\|_{\rm op}^2.$$
Its restriction to $\Theta\times\Theta$ defines the contamination modulus
$\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)$ through [[def-contamination-modulus]]. Suppose
$\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)<\infty$, $0\le M_0<\infty$, $0<c_0\le1$, and
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma\in\mathscr E_n}\sup_{\Sigma\in\Theta} P_\Sigma^{\otimes n}\{\ell(\Sigma,\widehat\Sigma)\ge M_0\}\ge c_0.$$
Then
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma\in\mathscr E_n}\sup_{\Sigma\in\Theta}\sup_Q P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}^{\otimes n} \left\{\ell(\Sigma,\widehat\Sigma)\ge \frac1{16}\bigl(M_0\vee\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)\bigr)\right\} \ge\min(c_0,1/2).$$

items.title: The Huber covariance contamination modulus has a quadratic lower bound

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, proof of Theorems 3.2 and 3.7

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the finite-dimensional Gaussian-law supplier; the covariance pair is explicit and uses no further choice.
items.statement:
For fixed $M>0$, $0\le\epsilon\le1$, and $p\ge1$, the squared operator
loss $L(\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1)=\|\Sigma_0-\Sigma_1\|_{\rm op}^2$ has
contamination modulus at least $c_M\epsilon^2$ on $\mathcal F_p(M)$ and on
$\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)$ for every $1\le s\le p/2$.

items.title: Operator error bound for the Gaussian Huber matrix-depth estimator

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Theorem 7.1 and proofs of Theorems 3.1 and 3.6

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the Gaussian Huber model. The comparison proof takes a Borel statistic as input and adds no choice.
items.statement:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent with common law
$P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$ from [[def-huber-covariance-model]], where
$\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)$, $0\le\epsilon<1/5$, $Q$ is arbitrary, and
$M>0$ is fixed. Let $\widehat\Gamma$ be a Borel measurable positive semidefinite symmetric matrix-valued statistic satisfying
$$D_U(\widehat\Gamma,P_n)\ge D_U(\beta\Sigma,P_n)$$
for every sample. This includes every measurable global maximizer and every measurable maximizer over a compact search class containing $\beta\Sigma$. For a direction family
$U=\bigcup_{j=1}^mV_{S_j}$ with $m\ge1$, nonempty $S_j\subseteq[p]$, integer
$r\ge1$, and $|S_j|\le r$, assume $0<\delta<1/2$ and
$C_1(r+\log(m/\delta))/n<1$ for a sufficiently large universal $C_1$.
Then, uniformly over $Q$ and $\Sigma$,
$$\sup_{u\in U}|u^T(\widehat\Gamma/\beta-\Sigma)u| \le C_M\left(\epsilon+\sqrt{\frac{r+\log(m/\delta)}n}\right)$$
with probability at least $1-2\delta$. Here $C_M$ depends only on the
fixed spectrum bound $M$.

This is a comparison bound. Existence of selectors is separate from this argument; the dense and block-sparse global and bounded-class selectors are proved in the local selection lemma.

items.title: Measurable selection of a matrix-depth maximizer

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §3.2

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through beta in the matrix-depth definition. The deterministic finite dyadic construction adds no choice principle.
items.statement:
For every nonempty finite sample, both the bounded-class and global dense
and block-sparse argmax correspondences in
[[def-matrix-depth-covariance-estimator]] admit Borel measurable selectors
as functions of the sample. The covariance output obtained by division by
$\beta$ is Borel as well. No computational feasibility is asserted.

items.title: Adaptive truncated covariance has a finite matrix-variance operator bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m\in\mathbb R^p$ be clean iid
observations with mean $\mu$, nonzero covariance $\Sigma$, and finite fourth
central moment. For the matrix variance in
[[def-matrix-variance-of-a-random-vector]], put
$$d=\frac{\sigma_0^2}{\|\Sigma\|^2},\qquad D=\max\left\{d,\left(\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma}{\sigma_0}\right)^2\right\}.$$
Suppose $\beta>1$, $0<\sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_0\le\sigma_{\max}$ and
$$m\ge10^{16}D\beta.$$
The same-sample pilot and original scale/selection rule of
[[alg-adaptive-truncated-covariance-estimator]] then satisfy
$$P\!\left(\|\widehat\Sigma^*-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}>18\sigma_0\sqrt{\frac\beta m}\right)\le5p\log_2\!\left(\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}\right)e^{-\beta}.$$
Here $p$ is ambient dimension; it is not the intrinsic ratio $d$. More
precisely, with $L_g=\log_2(2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min})$ and
$N_+=\lceil L_g\rceil-\lceil\log_2(\sigma_0/\sigma_{\min})\rceil$, the
failure bound is
$$\left[1+\frac{3p+1}{2}N_+\right]e^{-\beta}.$$
The trace-aware sample condition is sufficient, not necessary. All clean
finite-fourth-moment laws remain eligible; no coordinate independence,
kurtosis bound, contamination or replacement guarantee is imposed.
The broader uniform pilot-accuracy formula in
[[lem-fixed-scale-truncated-covariance-deviation]] can be used instead of
this sufficient sample condition whenever it establishes the same
fixed-scale radius for each required scale.

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, Theorem 2.1 and §4.3

items.title: Clean block-sparse Gaussian covariance has squared operator lower rate s log(ep/s) over n

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, proof of Theorem 3.7
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 5

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the finite-dimensional Gaussian-law supplier. Every packing used below is an explicit finite set and needs no further choice.
items.statement:
Fix $M>0$ and integers $1\le s\le p/2$. There are constants
$c_M,c_1>0$ such that if $s\log(ep/s)/n\le c_1$, then
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)} P_\Sigma^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \ge c_M\frac{s\log(ep/s)}n\right\}\ge c_1.$$
The infimum is over Borel maps $(\mathbb R^p)^n\to\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.
This is the
single-common-block class, not a row-sparsity class.

items.title: Clean Gaussian covariance has a capped squared operator lower rate

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, proof of Theorem 3.2
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 5

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the finite-dimensional Gaussian-law supplier. The sign families and finite codes are chosen from explicit finite sets, so they require no further choice.
items.statement:
Fix $M>0$. There are constants $c_M,c_1>0$ such that if $p/n\le c_1$,
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)} P_\Sigma^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \ge c_M\frac pn\right\}\ge c_1.$$
The infimum is over Borel maps $(\mathbb R^p)^n\to\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.
The constants
may depend on $M$, but not on $p$ or $n$.

In addition, there is $a_M>0$ such that for every $p,n\ge1$,
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)}P_\Sigma^{\otimes n}\left\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2\ge a_M\min\{1,p/n\}\right\}\ge c_1.$$
One may choose $0<c_1\le1/16$ and $a_M=\min\{c_Mc_1/2,M^2c_1/64\}$ after fixing the constants of the first assertion. Thus the original small-ratio lower bound is retained and the capped extension covers every dimension and sample size.

items.title: Dense Gaussian Huber covariance: high-probability upper and capped lower bounds

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Theorems 3.1, 3.2 and 5.1
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 5

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the Gaussian covariance model; the local error bounds and the contamination reduction add no choice.
items.statement:
Fix $M>0$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent with common law
$P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$ from [[def-huber-covariance-model]], where
$\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)$ and $Q$ is arbitrary. If $0\le\epsilon<1/5$,
$0<\delta<1/2$, and
$C_1(p+\log(1/\delta))/n<1$ for a sufficiently large universal $C_1$,
then every Borel measurable dense matrix-depth estimator, from either the global positive semidefinite correspondence or the bounded-class correspondence,
$\widehat\Sigma=\widehat\Gamma/\beta$ from
[[def-matrix-depth-covariance-estimator]] satisfies
$$\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \le C_M\left[\left(\frac pn\vee\epsilon^2\right) +\frac{\log(1/\delta)}n\right]$$
with probability at least $1-2\delta$, uniformly over $Q$ and
$\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)$.

Such Borel maximizing selectors exist by [[lem-measurable-matrix-depth-maximizer-selection]].

There are constants $c_M,c_M'>0$ such that for every $p,n\ge1$ and every $0\le\epsilon\le1$,
$$\inf_{\widetilde\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)}\sup_Q P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}^{\otimes n}\!\left\{ \|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \ge c_M\min\left\{1,\frac pn\vee\epsilon^2\right\}\right\}\ge c_M'.$$
The infimum is over all Borel maps $(\mathbb R^p)^n\to\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.
The constants may depend on $M$.

items.title: Single-block sparse Gaussian Huber covariance: high-probability upper and low-ratio lower bounds

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, Theorems 3.6, 3.7 and 5.1
Philippe Rigollet, 18.S997 High-Dimensional Statistics Lecture Notes, MIT OpenCourseWare, Chapter 5

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the Gaussian covariance model; the local error bounds and the contamination reduction add no choice.
items.statement:
Fix $M>0$ and an integer $1\le s\le p/2$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be
independent with common law $P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$ from
[[def-huber-covariance-model]], where $\Sigma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)$ and
$Q$ is arbitrary. If $0\le\epsilon<1/5$, $0<\delta<1/2$, and
$$C_1\frac{s\log(ep/s)+\log(1/\delta)}n<1$$
for sufficiently large universal $C_1$, then every Borel measurable restricted matrix-depth estimator, from either the global single-block correspondence or the bounded-class correspondence,
$\widehat\Sigma=\widehat\Gamma/\beta$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \le C_M\left[\left(\frac{s\log(ep/s)}n\vee\epsilon^2\right) +\frac{\log(1/\delta)}n\right]$$
with probability at least $1-2\delta$, uniformly over $Q$ and
$\Sigma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)$.

Such Borel maximizing selectors exist by [[lem-measurable-matrix-depth-maximizer-selection]].

There are constants $c_M,c_M',c_1>0$ such that whenever
$s\log(ep/s)/n\le c_1$, for every $0\le\epsilon\le1$,
$$\inf_{\widetilde\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_{p,s}(M)}\sup_Q P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}^{\otimes n}\!\left\{ \|\widetilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2 \ge c_M\left(\frac{s\log(ep/s)}n\vee\epsilon^2\right)\right\}\ge c_M'.$$
The constants may depend on $M$. The class is one common correlated block,
not a row-sparsity class. The infimum is over all Borel maps
$(\mathbb R^p)^n\to\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.

title: Robust Covariance and Sparse Robust Estimation — Examples

items.title: Matrix variance need not dominate trace covariance times operator norm

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, Corollary 5.1

items.statement:
For every centered square-integrable random vector $Z$ with finite fourth
moment, the matrix variance
$$\sigma_0^2=\left\|\mathbb E[\|Z\|_2^2ZZ^T]\right\|_{\rm op}$$
is at least $\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}$, where
$\Sigma=\mathbb E[ZZ^T]$.

items.title: A polynomial-tail law with finite matrix variance

references.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions, §2

items.statement:
For $r>1$ let $\zeta(r)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}k^{-r}$. On
$\Omega=\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ with its power-set sigma-algebra,
let
$$P=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{2\zeta(6)k^6}(\delta_k+\delta_{-k}).$$
Set $X(\omega)=\omega$. Thus the two atoms $k,-k$ each have mass
$1/(2\zeta(6)k^6)$.

items.title: A bounded covariance class forces a capped lower rate
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the Gaussian Huber model; the deterministic zero-estimator calculation adds no choice.
items.statement:
For fixed $M>0$, there are positive constants $C_M,c_0$ such that for every $p,n\ge1$ and $0\le\epsilon\le1$,
$$\inf_{\widehat\Sigma}\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal F_p(M)}\sup_Q P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}^{\otimes n}\left\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2\ge C_M\bigl((p/n)\vee\epsilon^2\bigr)\right\}\ge c_0,$$
where the infimum ranges over all Borel matrix-valued estimators.

items.title: Intrinsic matrix variance alone does not control pilot-centered covariance truncation
items.statement:
There is a universal $C$ such that every clean iid finite-fourth-moment law
with nonzero covariance, intrinsic matrix-variance ratio
$d=\sigma_0^2/\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}^2$ and $m\ge Cd\beta$ has the
following guarantees for the same-sample geometric-median pilot procedure:
the fixed-scale error is at most $3\sigma\sqrt{\beta/m}$, with failure
at most $5d e^{-\beta}$, and the adaptive error is at most
$18\sigma_0\sqrt{\beta/m}$, with failure at most
$5d\log_2(2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min})e^{-\beta}$.
Even replacing the failure prefactor $d$ by ambient dimension $p$ does not
make the $Cd\beta$ sample condition sufficient in general.

references.title: Minsker and Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions

items.statement:
Let $p=4$, $s=2$, $M=2$, $\epsilon=1/10$, and
$$\Sigma=I_4+\frac14(e_1e_2^T+e_2e_1^T),\qquad Q=\delta_0.$$
The observations have law $P_{\epsilon,\Sigma,Q}$.

references.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model, §2

items.statement:
Let $p=2$, $M=2$, $\epsilon=1/10$,
$$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/4\\1/4&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad Q=\delta_{(2,0)}.$$
Take independent observations with the Gaussian Huber law
